verses: طه
مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰٓ
إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
تَنزِيلًا مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ
إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ
إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ
إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ
فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرْدَىٰ
وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ
قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَىٰ
قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ
وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى
ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى
يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
هَٰرُونَ أَخِى
ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى
وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى
كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا
وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا
إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا
قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ
إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ

أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى
ٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكْرِى
ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ
إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَٰبٍ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى
ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ
كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَٰمَكُمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى
قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى
فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
فَتَنَٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ خِيفَةً مُّوسَىٰ
قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ
وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ
قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
وَمَن يَأْتِهِۦ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ
فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ
كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ
وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ
قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى
قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ
أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا
وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ
قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟
أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى
قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَٰسَٰمِرِىُّ
قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى

قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا
إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًا
كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًا
مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا
خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًا
يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا
يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا
نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا
وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًا
فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا
لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَآ أَمْتًا
يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا
يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُۥ قَوْلًا
يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًا
وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا
وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا
وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا
فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا
وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُۥ عَزْمًا
وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ
وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ
فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ
فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةً ضَنكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ أَعْمَىٰ
قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًا
قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ
وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِى مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى
فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ ءَانَآئِ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ
وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًا مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ
وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْـَٔلُكَ رِزْقًا نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ
وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
وَلَوْ أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُم بِعَذَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِهِۦ لَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن نَّذِلَّ وَنَخْزَىٰ
قُلْ كُلٌّ مُّتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ

leads.title: Jeroboam's golden calves and rival cult ↔ Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt (weight 6.3); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Pair score 11.0.

Only in Jeroboam's golden calves and rival cult: King invents a rival pilgrimage festival on the fifteenth of the eighth month, a month 'he devised from his own heart'; Postponing a sacred month (al-nasi', intercalation) is an increase in unbelief; King appoints priests from all the people who are not Levites; An altar built outside the central sanctuary almost leads to civil war; King sets up two golden calves at Bethel and Dan so the people need not go to Jerusalem.

Only in Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf: Aaron explains he feared being blamed for dividing the children of Israel; Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns; The calf is burned and its remains scattered in the sea (yamm); The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast; The calf-maker took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger and cast it in; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment; In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother'; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: Contest on Mount Carmel ↔ Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1). Pair score 5.1.

Only in Contest on Mount Carmel: Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob; Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God; The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon; Prophets of Baal limp-dance around the altar and gash themselves with swords and lances till blood flows; Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken; Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle; The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!'; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts]; Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water; 'How long will you hop between two branches? If YHWH is God, follow him; if Baal, follow him'; A single prophet of YHWH stands against 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah; and 10 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes; Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life'; Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' Only in Manna and quail; the first Sabbath: God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert; Food is given daily, a day's portion at a time, to test obedience; A double portion of manna falls or is gathered on the sixth day; The people eat manna or wander for forty years in the wilderness; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; Manna kept overnight breeds worms and stinks; A jar of manna preserved before the testimony for future generations; Manna described: like coriander seed, look of bdellium, taste of oil cakes, falls with the dew; Manna appears as a fine flaky layer like hoarfrost when the dew lifts; Ungathered manna melts when the sun grows hot; Explanatory gloss defining a measure (an omer is a tenth of an ephah); The people grumble against their leaders about food or water; Each gathers an omer per person; the one who gathers much has no excess, the one who gathers little no lack; Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp; Those who go out to gather on the Sabbath find nothing; Manna kept for the Sabbath does not spoil or breed worms; Seventh-day rest declared holy to God, with no gathering or going out.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Destroyed generations, patience, prayer times and waiting: Appeal to 'the former scrolls' (al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā) as evidence; God's name is praised from the rising of the sun to its setting; God's name is praised from the rising of the sun to its setting [divergence between the texts]; Glorify your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, in the night and after prostrations; Punishment is delayed only because of a word that went before from God and an appointed term; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; God does not punish a people before sending a messenger, lest they plead they had none.

matches.note: Setting and motive change. Exod: Moses alone with Jethro's flock at har hāʾĕlōhîm, drawn by a wonder, hassəneh bōʿēr bāʾēš wəhassəneh ʾênennû ʾukkāl ... ʾāsurâ-nnāʾ wəʾerʾeh. Q: Moses traveling with his family (qāla li-ahlihi mkuthū) sees a fire and goes for a practical need, la-ʿallī ātīkum minhā bi-qabasin aw ajidu ʿalā n-nāri hudā. Q 20 does not mention the unconsumed bush.

matches.label: The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā
matches.note: God's self-introduction. Exod: ancestral God and the revealed name, ʾānōkî ʾĕlōhê ʾābîkā ʾĕlōhê ʾabrāhām ... ʾehyeh ʾăšer ʾehyeh ... YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăbōtêkem ... zeh-ššəmî ləʿōlām. leads.title: The golden calf ↔ Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf
leads.summary: 4 correspondences read side by side: 4 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt (weight 6.3); A golden calf is made from the people's gold earrings (weight 6.3). Pair score 38.9.

Only in The golden calf: Aaron builds an altar before the calf and proclaims a feast to YHWH; Intercessor reminds God of his oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; The people eat, drink and rise up to revel before the idol; The prophet's delay on the mountain makes the people lose faith; Whether the calf is a god that leads the people [response between the texts]; Israel asks its leader to make them a god [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; Who makes the golden calf and from what [divergence between the texts]; If God willed he could remove you and bring a new creation; and 3 more.

Only in Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf: Aaron explains he feared being blamed for dividing the children of Israel; Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns; The calf is burned and its remains scattered in the sea (yamm); The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast; The calf-maker took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger and cast it in; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment; In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother'; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother' [divergence between the texts]; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf; and 4 more.

matches.label: A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf
matches.note: Who makes the calf. Exod: Aaron, at the people's demand, qûm ʿăśēh-lānû ʾĕlōhîm ... pārəqû nizmê hazzāhāb ... wayyiṣar ʾōtô baḥereṭ wayyaʿăśēhû ʿēgel massēkâ. Q: al-Sāmirī, wa-aḍallahumu s-Sāmiriyy ... fa-kadhālika alqā s-Sāmiriyyu fa-akhraja lahum ʿijlan jasadan lahu khuwār. Aaron is cleared and a new agent is brought in, who gives his own motive: baṣurtu bi-mā lam yabṣurū bihi fa-qabaḍtu qabḍatan min athari r-rasūl.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם עֲשֵׂה לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי זֶ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי
וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ

matches.label: Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns
matches.note: Reversal. Exod: Aaron builds the altar before the calf and proclaims ḥag laYHWH māḥār. Q: Aaron warns them, yā qawmi innamā futintum bihi wa-inna rabbakumu r-Raḥmānu fa-ttabiʿūnī, and the people refuse, lan nabraḥa ʿalayhi ʿākifīna ḥattā yarjiʿa ilaynā Mūsā.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר
وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ

matches.label: The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt
matches.note: ʾēlleh ʾĕlōhêkā yiśrāʾēl ʾăšer heʿĕlûkā mēʾereṣ miṣrāyim; hādhā ilāhukum wa-ilāhu Mūsā fa-nasiya. Exod has a plural 'gods' credited with the exodus; Q has 'your god and Moses' god, whom he forgot', making Moses' absence on the mountain into forgetfulness.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ לוֹ֙ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ ל֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ

matches.label: God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment
matches.note: God tells Moses on the mountain what the people have done. Exod: lek-rēd kî šiḥēt ʿamməkā ... wəʿattâ hannîḥâ llî wəyiḥar-ʾappî bāhem waʾăkallēm, and Moses intercedes, lāmmâ YHWH yeḥĕreh ʾappəkā. Q: God asks mā aʿjalaka ʿan qawmika and says fa-innā qad fatannā qawmaka, the people tested by God himself. There is no threat to destroy them and no intercession.

passages.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה לֶךְ רֵ֕ד כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם קְשֵׁה עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא
וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל
وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ
قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כָּל הָעָ֔ם אֶת נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹֽן
וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם
قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ

leads.title: Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer ↔ Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The idol calf is a body that makes a lowing sound (khuwar) (weight 6.3). Pair score 26.4.

Only in Tablets broken, calf destroyed, Levites slaughter, Moses' offer: Aaron excuses himself: the people pressed him and the calf came out of the fire; The people run wild and become a derision to their enemies; God strikes the people with plague for idolatry; The prophet asks to be blotted from God's book if the people are not forgiven; The noise of the idolatrous revelry is mistaken for the sound of battle; The tablets are written on both sides by God; The leader calls 'Who is for YHWH? To me!' and a group rallies; Aaron answers Moses' rebuke over the calf [divergence between the texts]; Israel made to drink the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; God erases what he wills and confirms, and with him is the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab); God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; The idol is burned, ground to powder, scattered on water and the people made to drink it; and 13 more.

Only in Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf: Aaron explains he feared being blamed for dividing the children of Israel; Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns; The calf is burned and its remains scattered in the sea (yamm); The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast; The calf-maker took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger and cast it in; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment; In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother'; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf; A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת הָעֵ֨גֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּטְחַ֖ן עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר דָּ֑ק וַיִּ֨זֶר֙ עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

matches.label: In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother'
matches.note: Exod: Moses accuses Aaron, mah-ʿāśâ ləkā hāʿām hazzeh kî-hēbēʾtā ʿālāyw ḥăṭāʾâ gədōlâ, and Aaron blames the people and the fire, wāʾašlikēhû bāʾēš wayyēṣēʾ hāʿēgel hazzeh. Q: Moses seizes him, and Aaron pleads yabnaʾumma lā taʾkhudh bi-liḥyatī wa-lā bi-raʾsī innī khashītu an taqūla farraqta bayna banī Isrāʾīl. Aaron's excuse changes from the calf 'coming out' by itself to fear of schism.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֔ן מֶֽה עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי הֵבֵ֥אתָ עָלָ֖יו חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדֹלָֽה
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אַל יִ֥חַר אַ֖ף אֲדֹנִ֑י אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא
וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה
قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟
أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى
قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى

matches.label: The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast
matches.note: Punishment. Exod: the Levites kill about three thousand, mî laYHWH ʾēlāy ... hirgû ʾîš-ʾet-ʾāḥîw. Q: no massacre; the one guilty man is sent away as an outcast, fa-dhhab fa-inna laka fī l-ḥayāti an taqūla lā misās, with a further appointment (mawʿidan lan tukhlafah).

passages.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׂ֥ימוּ אִישׁ חַרְבּ֖וֹ עַל יְרֵכ֑וֹ עִבְר֨וּ וָשׁ֜וּבוּ מִשַּׁ֤עַר לָשַׁ֨עַר֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהִרְג֧וּ אִֽישׁ אֶת אָחִ֛יו וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת קְרֹבֽוֹ
וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ

قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

leads.title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa
leads.summary: 5 correspondences read side by side: 4 deliberately changed, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 48.6.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts]; and 11 more.

Only in Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa: The Hour is coming; God almost keeps it hidden so each soul is repaid for its striving; Prophet prays for his chest to be expanded and the knot of his tongue untied; Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there [divergence between the texts]; The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; Hero told to remove his sandals because the place is holy ground; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוָ֖ה מזה מַה זֶּ֣ה בְיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מַטֶּֽה
وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ

matches.label: Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign
matches.note: Exod: wəhinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat kaššāleg, a leprous hand, given so that the people will believe (ləmaʿan yaʾămînû). Q: takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾ, white 'without harm', which denies the disease, and given li-nuriyaka min āyātinā l-kubrā, a sign for Moses himself.

passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּקֹלִ֑י כִּ֣י יֹֽאמְר֔וּ לֹֽא נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה
לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב
וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּבֵ֥א יָד֖וֹ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וַיּ֣וֹצִאָ֔הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה יָד֖וֹ מְצֹרַ֥עַת כַּשָּֽׁלֶג
وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى

matches.label: Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips'
matches.note: Exod: speech trouble is an objection to the call, lōʾ ʾîš dəbārîm ʾānōkî ... kî kəbad-peh ûkəbad lāšôn ʾānōkî ... šəlaḥ-nāʾ bəyad-tišlāḥ, and God rebukes him, mî śām peh lāʾādām. Q: it is a prayer, rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī ... wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī, granted at once, qad ūtīta suʾlaka yā Mūsā.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל יְהוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ אֶל עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֧י כְבַד פֶּ֛ה וּכְבַ֥ד לָשׁ֖וֹן אָנֹֽכִי
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒ א֚וֹ מִֽי יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָֽה
וְעַתָּ֖ה לֵ֑ךְ וְאָנֹכִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִם פִּ֔יךָ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּֽר
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى

matches.label: The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission
matches.note: Who initiates, and the mood. Exod: God imposes Aaron in anger, wayyiḥar-ʾap YHWH bəmōšeh ... hălōʾ ʾahărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wəhāyâ-hûʾ yihyeh-ləkā ləpeh wəʾattâ tihyeh-lô lēʾlōhîm. Q: Moses asks for him, wa-jʿal lī wazīran min ahlī Hārūna akhī ushdud bihi azrī wa-ashrikhu fī amrī, so that they may glorify God much (kay nusabbiḥaka kathīrā). No anger, and no 'as God'.

passages.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֨ף יְהוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי דַבֵּ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר ה֑וּא וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ
וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִ֑יו וְאָנֹכִ֗י אֶֽהְיֶ֤ה עִם פִּ֨יךָ֙ וְעִם פִּ֔יהוּ וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֽׂוּן
וְדִבֶּר ה֥וּא לְךָ֖ אֶל הָעָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה הוּא֙ יִֽהְיֶה לְּךָ֣ לְפֶ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים
وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
هَٰرُونَ أَخِى
ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى

matches.label: A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff
matches.note: hašlîkēhû ʾarṣâ ... wayhî lənāḥāš wayyānos mōšeh mippānāyw ... šəlaḥ yādəkā weʾĕḥōz bizənābô; alqihā ... fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā, qāla khudhhā wa-lā takhaf sa-nuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā: thrown down, it becomes a snake; he is told to take it and it turns back. Moses flees in Exod; in Q he is told 'do not fear'.

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיַּ֣חֲזֶק בּ֔וֹ וַיְהִ֥י לְמַטֶּ֖ה בְּכַפּֽוֹ

قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' (weight 6.3); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4). Pair score 24.7.

Only in First audience with Pharaoh; bricks without straw: Slaves must make the same quota of bricks while gathering their own straw; The oppressed blame the deliverer for making things worse; Prophet complains to God that his mission has only made things worse; Foreign taskmasters over native foremen who are beaten for unmet quotas; Tyrant accuses the oppressed of idleness for wanting to worship; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh gathers the people and proclaims 'I am your Lord most high' [divergence between the texts]; Pharaoh: 'I show you only what I see, and guide you only to the right path'; Request for a three days' journey into the wilderness to sacrifice; Pharaoh's question about, or claim to know, the god of Moses [divergence between the texts]; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing.

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'
matches.note: Title and purpose change. Exod: kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl šallaḥ ʾet-ʿammî wəyāḥōggû lî bammidbār ... ʾĕlōhê hāʿibrîm niqrāʾ ʿālênû ... wənizbəḥâ: the God of Israel, of the Hebrews, wants a festival and sacrifice three days into the wilderness. Q: innā rasūlā rabbika, 'messengers of your Lord', Pharaoh's own Lord, and the purpose is release from oppression, fa-arsil maʿanā banī Isrāʾīla wa-lā tuʿadhdhibhum. Q adds wa-s-salāmu ʿalā mani ttabaʿa l-hudā.

passages.text: וְאַחַ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֑ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת עַמִּ֔י וְיָחֹ֥גּוּ לִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּֽר
וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָעִבְרִ֖ים נִקְרָ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ נֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֡א דֶּרֶךְ֩ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֜ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וְנִזְבְּחָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ פֶּ֨ן יִפְגָּעֵ֔נוּ בַּדֶּ֖בֶר א֥וֹ בֶחָֽרֶב
فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

matches.label: King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?'
matches.note: mî YHWH ʾăšer ʾešmaʿ bəqōlô ... lōʾ yādaʿtî ʾet-YHWH, and Moses gives no answer; fa-man rabbukumā yā Mūsā, and Moses answers with a creation creed, rabbunā lladhī aʿṭā kulla shayʾin khalqahu thumma hadā. Exod's question is about an unknown name; Q's is about a Lord, and the answer is a universal creator. Exod's sequel, the harsher labor (bricks without straw), is left out.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה מִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹל֔וֹ לְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֤א יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה וְגַ֥ם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֲשַׁלֵּֽחַ
قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ

matches.label: The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron
matches.note: Exod: failing at the lice, the magicians concede, ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, but nothing follows and Pharaoh stays hard. Q: defeated at the staff, they fall prostrate, āmannā bi-rabbi Hārūna wa-Mūsā, and become martyrs facing amputation and crucifixion, fa-qḍi mā anta qāḍin innamā taqḍī hādhihi l-ḥayāta d-dunyā. Exod's limited acknowledgment becomes full conversion.

passages.text: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה
וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ
قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ

leads.title: The heated oven, the silly dove and the calf of Samaria ↔ Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A man called al-Sāmirī leads Israel astray and makes the calf (weight 6.7); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 4.7). Pair score 11.4.

Only in The heated oven, the silly dove and the calf of Samaria: The calf of Samaria, made by a craftsman, is no god and will be broken to pieces; Court conspirators are like a heated oven; they devour their judges and their kings fall; The people are like a deceitful (slack) bow; Ephraim is a cake not turned (half-baked); God spreads his net over the people and brings them down like birds of the sky; Grey hairs are sprinkled on him and he does not know it; They made kings, but not by me; princes, but I did not know it; Though God writes for him the many things of his Torah, they are counted as something strange; Ephraim is like a silly dove, calling to Egypt and going to Assyria; They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind; Ephraim like a wild ass wandering alone, hiring lovers; Blow the shofar in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah, sound the alarm at Beth-aven; and 1 more.

Only in Moses hastens to the appointment; the Samiri and the calf: Aaron explains he feared being blamed for dividing the children of Israel; Aaron warns the people against the calf; they refuse to stop until Moses returns; The calf is burned and its remains scattered in the sea (yamm); The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast; The calf-maker took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger and cast it in; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment; In anger Moses seizes his brother by the beard and head; Aaron pleads 'son of my mother'; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream; Calf burned, ground to dust, and the dust thrown into the stream [divergence between the texts]; The calf-maker is condemned to say all his life 'No touching!' (lā misās), an outcast [divergence between the texts]; The calf is hailed as the god who brought Israel out of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God asks Moses why he hastened ahead of his people to the appointment [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

leads.title: The mountain of the Lord's house; the Day of YHWH against all that is proud ↔ The trumpet, the leveled mountains and the hushed judgment
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: On the day of judgment voices are hushed before the Merciful; only a faint murmur is heard (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in The mountain of the Lord's house; the Day of YHWH against all that is proud: Stop trusting man, who has only breath in his nostrils; On that day people throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats and flee into clefts of the rocks; Foreign priests and diviners advise how to appease the God of Israel; On God's day all that is lofty (cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan, towers, ships of Tarshish) is brought low and God alone exalted; In the latter days the mountain of God's house will be raised above all mountains and all nations will stream to it; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness; Nations will beat swords into plowshares and spears into pruning hooks and learn war no more; 'From Zion shall go forth Torah and the word of YHWH from Jerusalem'; God shatters the ships of Tarshish with an east wind; God the Judge is called to judge between two nations; People hide in caves, thickets, rocks and pits from an invading army; Prophecy concerning 'the end of days'; and 2 more.

Only in The trumpet, the leveled mountains and the hushed judgment: On the last day God scatters the mountains as dust and leaves a level, featureless plain; The guilty are gathered on that day blue-eyed or bleary (zurq); The prophet is told not to hasten with the recitation before its revelation is complete; Every valley lifted up, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked made straight for God's coming; Every valley lifted up, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked made straight for God's coming [divergence between the texts]; At the resurrection people think they tarried only ten days, or a day, or part of a day; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); The revelation is sent down as an Arabic Quran; The trumpet (ṣūr) is blown and the dead are gathered; Intercession avails only for whom God permits.

leads.title: Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail ↔ The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Taberah, the craving, the seventy elders and the quail: Fire from God burns part of the camp for complaint; Spirit rests on people and they prophesy (ecstatically); A 'rabble' or mixed crowd among the people instigates sin; Leader refuses to silence prophets outside the sanctioned place: 'would all were prophets'; Bird-meat as desired food: punished or granted [contrast between the texts]; Leader doubts God can supply; God replies 'Is my hand too short?' [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Craved food granted, then plague strikes while meat is still in their mouths; Leader protests he did not conceive or bear the people to carry them like a nurse; Exhausted leader asks God to kill him; Manna described: like coriander seed, look of bdellium, taste of oil cakes, falls with the dew; and 8 more.

Only in The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna: The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side [divergence between the texts]; King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots; A mountain called the mountain of God; Manna named from the people's question 'What is it?' (man hu); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives.

leads.title: End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section) ↔ Destroyed generations, patience, prayer times and waiting
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in End of the Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel section): Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, lest YHWH see it, be displeased and turn his anger from him; Fear YHWH and the king, and do not mix with those who seek change; By wisdom a house is built and by knowledge its rooms are filled with precious riches; Rescue those being taken to death; do not say 'we did not know', for the weigher of hearts knows; The righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in calamity; He who plans evil will be called a master of schemes (ba'al mezimmot); Eat honey, my son, for it is good; so is wisdom sweet to your soul; Wisdom is too high (like corals, ra'mot) for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the gate; Do not envy sinners or evildoers, for there is a future (aharit) and your hope will not be cut off; Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and heart will be questioned; All a man's ways seem pure in his eyes, but YHWH weighs the spirits (hearts); From the bee's belly comes a drink of many colors in which is healing for people; and 4 more.

Only in Destroyed generations, patience, prayer times and waiting: Appeal to 'the former scrolls' (al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā) as evidence; God's name is praised from the rising of the sun to its setting; God's name is praised from the rising of the sun to its setting [divergence between the texts]; Glorify your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, in the night and after prostrations; Punishment is delayed only because of a word that went before from God and an appointed term; The unbelievers demand: 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?'; The listeners walk among the dwellings of generations God destroyed, a sign; God does not punish a people before sending a messenger, lest they plead they had none.

leads.title: Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus ↔ Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians
leads.summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 10.2.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 31 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes; Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life'; Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Manna named from the people's question 'What is it?' (man hu) (weight 6.3); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side (weight 5.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 16.1.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 38 more.

Only in The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna: The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side [divergence between the texts]; King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots; A mountain called the mountain of God; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' passages.text: قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

sides.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). There are no curses on the woman (childbirth, 3:16) or the ground (3:17-19).

passages.text: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

sides.note: wəʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā ûbên hāʾiššâ ûbên zarʿăkā ûbên zarʿāh ... wayəšalləḥēhû ... waygāreš ʾet-hāʾādām; qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww. Enmity and expulsion. Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

passages.text: فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

sides.note: A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). passages.text: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ

فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

leads.title: Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues ↔ Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians
leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron (weight 6.3); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents (weight 6.0); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.6); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 45.6.

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God'; Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; The magicians' ropes and staffs appear by sorcery to be moving like snakes; Condemned believers tell the tyrant 'decree what you will; you can only decree for this worldly life'; Pharaoh threatens the converted magicians with cutting off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucifixion (on palm trunks); King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' [divergence between the texts]; God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?'; and 3 more.

leads.finding: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents

units.title: Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues
Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians

matches.label: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents

passages.text: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ نَحْنُ ٱلْمُلْقِينَ
قَالَ أَلْقُوا۟ فَلَمَّآ أَلْقَوْا۟ سَحَرُوٓا۟ أَعْيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَآءُو بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ

sides.note: Who throws the staff, and how. Exod: Aaron throws (wa-yyašlēkh ʾAhărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wa-yhî lə-tannîn); the magicians do the same (bə-lahăṭêhem kēn); and maṭṭēh-ʾAhărōn swallows their staffs (wa-yyivlaʿ). Q: Moses throws (fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿbānun mubīnun); the magicians offer him the first throw (immā an tulqiya); their act is siḥr that 'bewitched the people's eyes' (saḥarū aʿyuna l-nāsi), and Moses' staff talqafu mā yaʾfikūna. Aaron drops out of the act; the magic is illusion.

passages.text: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ

sides.note: Exod: Aaron's staff (wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayhî lətannîn), and the magicians really do the same, wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bəlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyihyû lətannînim, before wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. Q: Moses' staff (alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū), and the magicians' ropes and staffs only seem to move, yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥrihim annahā tasʿā. The actor and the reality of the rival magic both change.

matches.label: The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron

passages.text: وَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'

passages.text: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّى رَسُولٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
حَقِيقٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّآ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

sides.note: The sender's title and the demand. Exod: kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê Yiśrāʾēl šallaḥ ʾet-ʿammî wə-yāḥōggû lî bam-midbār; ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivrîm niqrāʾ ʿālênû, God of Israel and of the Hebrews, with a pretext of a three-day festival or sacrifice. Q: yā Firʿawnu innī rasūlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna ... fa-arsil maʿiya banī Isrāʾīla. 'The Lord of the worlds', with no festival or three-day journey, and 'the Children of Israel' instead of 'my people'. Pharaoh's 'who is YHWH?' (mî YHWH, 5:2) becomes in fa-ʾti bihā in kunta mina l-ṣādiqīn.

passages.text: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

sides.note: Title and purpose change. Exod: kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl šallaḥ ʾet-ʿammî wəyāḥōggû lî bammidbār ... ʾĕlōhê hāʿibrîm niqrāʾ ʿālênû ... wənizbəḥâ: the God of Israel, of the Hebrews, wants a festival and sacrifice three days into the wilderness. Q: innā rasūlā rabbika, 'messengers of your Lord', Pharaoh's own Lord, and the purpose is release from oppression, fa-arsil maʿanā banī Isrāʾīla wa-lā tuʿadhdhibhum. Q adds wa-s-salāmu ʿalā mani ttabaʿa l-hudā.

matches.label: The prophet's staff-serpent swallows the magicians' staff-serpents

passages.text: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ

sides.note: talqafu ma ya'fikun

passages.text: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ

matches.label: The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people

passages.text: وَقَالُوا۟ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ لِّتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلْجَرَادَ وَٱلْقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتٍ مُّفَصَّلَٰتٍ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا مُّجْرِمِينَ
فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلرِّجْزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ

sides.note: Who hardens the heart. Exod: first Pharaoh (wa-yyakhbēd Parʿōh ʾet-libbô gam bap-paʿam haz-zōʾt), then God (wa-yḥazzēq YHWH ʾet-lēv Parʿōh, 9:12). Q: mahmā taʾtinā bihi min āyatin li-tasḥaranā bihā fa-mā naḥnu laka bi-muʾminīna; fa-stakbarū wa-kānū qawman mujrimīna. Pharaoh's people are proud and break their word (yankuthūna). God never hardens them in this unit.

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ

sides.note: Exod: God hardens, waʾănî ʾaqšeh ʾet-lēb parʿōh wəhirbêtî ʾet-ʾōtōtay, and wayyeḥĕzaq lēb parʿōh ... kaʾăšer dibber YHWH. Q: Pharaoh himself refuses, wa-la-qad araynāhu āyātinā kullahā fa-kadhdhaba wa-abā, and God's hand in it is not stated.

matches.label: Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me'

passages.text: حَقِيقٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّآ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِبَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

sides.note: fa-arsil ma'iya bani isra'il

passages.text: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

sides.note: 'send the children of Israel with us and do not torment them'

matches.label: Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest

passages.text: قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرْسِلْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَٰحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ
قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى
فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ

matches.label: The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people

passages.text: وَقَالُوا۟ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ لِّتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ

قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِۦ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا۟ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ

leads.title: Sargon and Moses: the infant in the sealed basket
leads.summary: The Neo-Assyrian Sargon Birth Legend has a baby placed in a reed basket sealed with bitumen, set on the river, and raised by a water-drawer. Exodus 2 and the Quran's Moses (into al-yamm) share the motif.

passages.note: papyrus basket daubed with bitumen and pitch
passages.text: (2:1) וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת בַּת לֵוִֽי (2:2) וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים (2:3) וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר (2:4) וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ (2:5) וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ (2:6) וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה (2:7) וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד (2:8) וַתֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֑כִי וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ הָֽעַלְמָ֔ה וַתִּקְרָ֖א אֶת אֵ֥ם הַיָּֽלֶד (2:9) וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ (2:10) וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ

passages.note: cast into the tābūt and the yamm
passages.text: (20:38) إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ (20:39) أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ (28:7) وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ (28:8) فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ (28:9) وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:10) وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (28:11) وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:12) وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ (28:13) فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

leads.title: al-yamm: the sea word reserved for Moses
leads.summary: The Quran's usual word for sea is bahr, but al-yamm appears 8 times across 4 surahs, always in the Moses/Pharaoh narrative. It is the Semitic sea word shared with Hebrew yam, Ugaritic Yam, and Mandaic yama, and borrowed into New Kingdom Egyptian.

lexical.gloss: Sea, the sea god opposed to Baal

passages.note: Pharaoh's people drowned in the yamm
passages.text: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

passages.note: Infant Moses cast into the yamm (two occurrences)
passages.text: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

passages.note: The golden calf scattered into the yamm
passages.text: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا

evidence.text: 8 occurrences of the lemma, verified with the Quran word concordance (root ي م م); the other root hits are the unrelated verb tayammum (2:267, 4:43, 5:6).
Dispersion: 4 surahs (7, 20, 28, 51), 1 narrative. Concentrated in one story while spread across the text.
Synonym-choice skew: bahr is the general word for sea elsewhere in the Quran.
Egyptian ym is a Semitic loanword, so this is shared Semitic vocabulary fitting the Egyptian setting, not an Egyptian borrowing into Arabic.
